sentences.zh: 歸二年而京師陷。

translations.literal: Returned two years and the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after his return home, the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 宗周徒步荷戈，詣杭州，責巡撫黃鳴駿發喪討賊，鳴駿誡以鎮靜，宗周勃然曰：「君父變出非常，公專閫外，不思枕戈泣血，激勵同仇，顧藉口鎮靜，作遜避計耶？」

translations.literal: Zongzhou went on foot bearing weapons, proceeding to Hangzhou, reproaching Governor Huang Mingjun to raise mourning and attack the bandits; Mingjun admonished him to keep calm—Zongzhou flared up and said: "Sovereign and father transformed in extraordinary fashion, you hold authority outside the passes, not thinking to pillow weapons and weep blood, rousing shared enmity, yet taking calm as pretext, making a plan of yielding avoidance?"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou marched on foot with a weapon to Hangzhou and demanded that Governor Huang Mingjun proclaim the Emperor's death and raise troops against the rebels. Huang urged restraint. Zongzhou blazed with anger: "The throne itself has been overthrown, and you command the province—yet instead of taking up arms and weeping blood to rally vengeance, you cite 'restraint' as an excuse to do nothing?"

sentences.zh: 鳴駿唯唯。

translations.literal: Mingjun assented vaguely.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 明日，復趣之。

translations.literal: The next day, he again pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zongzhou pressed him again.

sentences.zh: 鳴駿曰：「發喪必待哀詔。」

translations.literal: Mingjun said: "Raising mourning must await the lament edict."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun said: "We cannot proclaim the funeral without an imperial mourning edict."

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「嘻，此何時也，安所得哀詔哉！」

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Alas, what time is this—where would one obtain a lament edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Good heavens—what moment is this, and where would such an edict come from!"

sentences.zh: 鳴駿乃發喪。

translations.literal: Mingjun thereupon raised mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun finally proclaimed the mourning.

sentences.zh: 問師期，則曰：「甲仗未具。」

translations.literal: Asking the date for dispatching troops, he then said: "Armor and weapons are not yet prepared."
translations.idiomatic: When asked when he would march, Huang said: "Our arms and armor are not yet ready."

sentences.zh: 宗周嘆曰：「嗟乎，是烏足與有為哉！」

translations.literal: Zongzhou sighed and said: "Alas, this one is not sufficient to achieve anything with!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou sighed: "Ah—this man is capable of nothing worth doing!"

sentences.zh: 乃與故侍郎朱大典，故給事中章正宸、熊汝霖召募義旅。

translations.literal: Thereupon with former Vice Minister Zhu Dadian, former Submitter of Petitions Zhang Zhenchen, and Xiong Rulin he recruited righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the former Vice Minister Zhu Dadian and the former palace advisers Zhang Zhenchen and Xiong Rulin in raising a volunteer army.

sentences.zh: 將發，而福王監國於南京，起宗周故官。

translations.literal: About to set out, yet the Prince of Fu supervised the state at Nanjing and restored Zongzhou to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were about to march, the Prince of Fu assumed regency at Nanjing and recalled Zongzhou to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 宗周以大仇未報，不敢受職，自稱草莽孤臣，疏陳時政，言：

translations.literal: Zongzhou, because the great vengeance was not yet repaid, dared not accept the office, styled himself a lone minister of the wilds, and in a memorial set forth current administration, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou declined the post while national vengeance remained unfulfilled, calling himself a private subject of the wilderness, and submitted a memorial on current policy, declaring:

sentences.zh: 今日大計，舍討賊復仇，無以表陛下渡江之心；

translations.literal: Today's great plan: apart from attacking bandits and revenging, there is no means to display Your Majesty's heart in crossing the river;
translations.idiomatic: The paramount task today is vengeance against the rebels—without it, Your Majesty's purpose in crossing the Yangtze cannot be made clear;

sentences.zh: 非毅然決策親征，無以作天下忠義之氣。

translations.literal: Unless one resolutely decides and personally campaigns, there is no way to rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing short of a resolute decision to lead the campaign in person can stir the empire's spirit of loyal service.

sentences.zh: 一曰據形勝以規進取。

translations.literal: First: rely on strategic terrain to plan advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: First, seize advantageous ground and plan the advance north.

sentences.zh: 江左非偏安之業，請進圖江北。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangtze are not a foundation for partial peace; I ask that you advance to contrive the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangtze is no place to settle for mere survival; I urge an active strategy to recover the north.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽號中都，東扼徐、淮，北控豫州，西顧荊、襄，而南去金陵不遠，請以駐親征之師。

translations.literal: Fengyang is called the Central Capital; east it throttles Xu and Huai, north it controls Yuzhou, west it looks to Jing and Xiang, and south it is not far from Jinling—I ask that the army of the personal campaign be stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang—the old "Central Capital"—commands Xuzhou and the Huai region to the east, Henan to the north, and Jingzhou and Xiangyang to the west, while lying close to Nanjing to the south. Station Your Majesty's expeditionary force there.

sentences.zh: 大小銓除，暫稱行在，少存臣子負罪引慝之心。

translations.literal: Great and small appointments and removals should for the time be styled as from the mobile court, so as to retain somewhat the heart of ministers bearing guilt and acknowledging faults.
translations.idiomatic: Keep all appointments provisional under a "mobile court" designation, preserving among your ministers some sense of shared guilt and penitence.

sentences.zh: 從此漸進，秦、晉、燕、齊必有響應而起者。

translations.literal: Advancing gradually from this, in Qin, Jin, Yan, and Qi there will surely be those who rise in response.
translations.idiomatic: Advance step by step from there, and Qin, Jin, Yan, and Qi will surely rally to the cause.

sentences.zh: 一曰重藩屏以資彈壓。

translations.literal: Second: strengthen the screen-barriers to supply suppression and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Second, strengthen the frontier defenses so they can actually hold the line.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚數百里，設兩節鉞，不能禦亂，爭先南下，致江北一塊土，拱手授賊。

translations.literal: For several hundred li in Huai and Yang, two military commissioners were set, yet could not repel disorder; each raced to flee south, causing the whole stretch of land north of the river to be handed over to bandits with clasped hands.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of miles along the Huai and Yang regions, two commissioners with full military authority were stationed—yet they could not repel the enemy. They raced each other south and surrendered the entire north bank without a fight.

sentences.zh: 督漕路振飛坐守淮城，久以家屬浮舟遠地，是倡之逃也；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of the Grain Transport Lu Zhenfei sat defending Huai city, long keeping his family on boats at a distance—this was initiating flight;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfei, commissioner of grain transport, held Huai city while keeping his family on boats far away—a clear signal that flight was acceptable;

sentences.zh: 於是鎮臣劉澤清、高傑遂有家屬寄江南之說。

translations.literal: Thus the garrison commanders Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie then had talk of sending their families to lodge south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison generals Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie were likewise sending their families south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 軍法臨陣脫逃者斬，臣謂一撫二鎮皆可斬也。

translations.literal: Military law holds that one who flees in battle is beheaded; I say the one governor and two garrison commanders may all be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Desertion on the battlefield is a capital offense. I say the governor and both garrison commanders all deserve execution.

sentences.zh: 一曰慎爵賞以肅軍情。

translations.literal: Third: be cautious with ranks and rewards to stern the military morale.
translations.idiomatic: Third, review ennoblements and rewards carefully to restore military discipline.

sentences.zh: 請分別各帥封賞，孰當孰濫，輕則收侯爵，重則奪伯爵。

translations.literal: I ask to distinguish the enfeoffments and rewards of each commander—who deserved them and who received them excessively; lightly, strip marquisates; heavily, revoke earldoms.
translations.idiomatic: Review every commander's titles and rewards: distinguish the deserved from the gratuitous. Strip lesser offenders of their marquisates; revoke earldoms from the worst.

sentences.zh: 夫以左帥之恢復而封，高、劉之敗逃亦封，又誰不當封者？

translations.literal: Now if the Left Marshal was enfeoffed for recovery, while Gao and Liu were also enfeoffed for defeat and flight—who then would not deserve enfeoffment?
translations.idiomatic: If the Left Marshal was ennobled for recovering territory while Gao and Liu were rewarded for defeat and flight, who would not claim a title?

sentences.zh: 武臣既濫，文臣隨之，外臣既濫，中珰隨之，恐天下聞而解體也。

translations.literal: Once military ministers are excessive, civil ministers follow; once external ministers are excessive, palace eunuchs follow—I fear the empire will hear of it and disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: Indiscriminate rewards to generals invite the same from civil officials, and from regional officials to palace eunuchs. The empire will lose heart when it sees this.

sentences.zh: 一曰核舊官以立臣紀。

translations.literal: Fourth: verify former officials to establish the standard of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, audit former officials and restore ministerial standards.

sentences.zh: 燕京既破，有受偽官而叛者，有受偽官而逃者，有在封守而逃者，有奉使命而逃者，法皆不赦。

translations.literal: After Yanjing was fallen, there were those who accepted false appointments and rebelled, those who accepted false appointments and fled, those who were in garrison and fled, and those who bore missions and fled—the law pardons none.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Beijing, some took offices under the puppet regime and rebelled; some took such offices and fled; some abandoned their posts; some abandoned imperial missions. None deserve pardon.

sentences.zh: 亟宜分別定罪，為戒將來。

translations.literal: They should urgently be distinguished and sentenced, as a warning for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment should be swift and differentiated, as a warning for the future.

sentences.zh: 至於偽命南下，徘徊順逆之間，實繁有徒；

translations.literal: As for false orders coming south, wavering between submission and resistance, they are truly numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Many more accepted the rebel regime's appointments in the south and wavered between loyalty and surrender;

sentences.zh: 必且倡為曲說，以惑人心，尤宜誅絕。

translations.literal: They will surely promote crooked explanations to bewilder people's hearts—they should especially be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely spin excuses to confuse the people. These too must be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He continued:

sentences.zh: 當賊入秦流晉，漸過畿南，遠近洶洶，獨大江南北晏然，而二三督撫不聞遣一騎以壯聲援，賊遂得長驅犯闕。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Qin and flowed through Jin, gradually passing south of the capital region, near and far were in uproar, yet south of the Yangtze alone was tranquil; two or three governors and grand coordinators never sent a single rider to bolster support—and the bandits were thus able to drive straight to violate the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels swept through Shaanxi and Shanxi toward the capital, panic spread everywhere—yet the Jiangnan region sat undisturbed while governors and commissioners failed to send a single rider to aid the capital. The rebels rode straight to the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 坐視君父之危亡而不救，則封疆諸臣之當誅者一。

translations.literal: Sitting and watching the sovereign and father in peril and death without rescue—that is the first reason frontier ministers deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Standing idle while the emperor and dynasty perished—that is the first count against the frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 兇問已確，諸臣奮戈而起，決一戰以贖前愆，自當不俟朝食。

translations.literal: Once evil tidings were confirmed, ministers should have grasped weapons and risen, deciding one battle to redeem former faults—they should naturally not wait for morning meal.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dreadful news was confirmed, ministers should have seized their arms and fought immediately to redeem themselves—not even waiting for breakfast.

sentences.zh: 方且仰聲息於南中，爭言固圉之策，卸兵權於閫外，首圖定策之功，則封疆諸臣之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Yet they were leaning on breath and life in the south, contending to speak of strategies to secure the border, shedding military authority outside the command, seeking first credit for settling policy—that is another reason frontier ministers deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they looked to Nanjing for safety, quarreled over defensive strategies, shirked military responsibility to outsiders, and fought over credit for policy decisions—that is another count against them.

sentences.zh: 新朝既立之後，謂宜不俟終日，首遣北伐之師。

translations.literal: After the new dynasty was established, it was said one should not wait a full day but first dispatch northern-expedition armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new court was established, a northern expedition should have been launched the very same day.

sentences.zh: 不然，則亟馳一介，間道北進，檄燕中父老，起塞上名王，哭九廟，厝梓宮，訪諸王。

translations.literal: Otherwise, then urgently send one envoy by hidden route northward, proclaim to the elders of Yan, raise the famed princes of the frontier passes, mourn the nine temples, lay out the imperial coffin, and seek out the imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: At minimum, send an envoy by secret route north: rally the elders of Yan, summon the princes of the frontier, mourn the ancestral temples, recover the emperor's coffin, and find surviving members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 更不然，則起閩帥鄭芝龍，以海師下直沽，九邊督鎮合謀共奮，事或可為。

translations.literal: If still not so, then raise the Fujian commander Zheng Zhilong, with sea forces descend to Zhigu, and the nine frontier governors and garrisons conspire together to exert effort—the matter may yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Better still, mobilize Zheng Zhilong of Fujian: sail a fleet to Tianjin while the frontier governors and garrisons coordinate a rising—the cause might yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 而諸臣計不出此，則舉朝謀國不忠之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers' plans did not go beyond this—that is yet another reason the whole court, in scheming for the state disloyally, deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: The court conceived none of these plans—another count of disloyalty against the ministers.

sentences.zh: 罪廢諸臣，量從昭雪，自應援先帝遺詔及之，今乃概用新恩。

translations.literal: Ministers punished and dismissed should, according to measure, be cleared; they should naturally be reached through citing the former emperor's testament—yet now new grace is applied across the board.
translations.idiomatic: Officials punished and dismissed should have been restored according to the late emperor's will. Instead blanket amnesties have been granted.

sentences.zh: 誅閹定案，前後詔書鶻突，勢必彪虎之類，盡從平反而後已，則舉朝謀國不忠之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Cases fixing guilt on eunuchs—edicts before and after were incoherent; inevitably men like Biao Hu would all be reversed until done—another reason the whole court deserves execution for disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The verdicts against the eunuchs have been overturned by contradictory edicts. Rapacious figures of that ilk will all be rehabilitated—yet another count of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日問罪，當自中外諸臣不職者始。

translations.literal: Your subject says that today's assignment of guilt should begin with incompetent ministers at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: I say accountability should begin with every negligent minister, at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔納其言，宣付史館，中外為悚動。

translations.literal: An edict accepted his words and ordered them proclaimed to the Historical Archives; at home and abroad there was startled trembling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial and ordered it deposited in the Historical Archives. Court and country were shaken.

sentences.zh: 而馬士英、高傑、劉澤清恨甚，滋欲殺宗周矣。

translations.literal: But Ma Shi Ying, Gao Jie, and Liu Zeqing hated deeply and increasingly wished to kill Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying, Gao Jie, and Liu Zeqing were enraged and increasingly bent on killing Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗周連疏請告不得命，遂抗疏劾士英，言：

translations.literal: Zongzhou repeatedly memorialized requesting leave but received no approval; then he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Shi Ying, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou repeatedly requested leave without success, then submitted a bold memorial impeaching Ma Shi Ying, declaring:

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飛淮甸，天實予之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's dragon flight in the Huai region—Heaven truly granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's accession in the Huai region was Heaven's own gift.

sentences.zh: 乃有扈蹕微勞，入內閣，進中樞，宮銜世蔭，晏然當之不疑者，非士英乎？

translations.literal: Yet there was one with slight merit in escorting the imperial carriage who entered the Grand Secretariat, advanced to the central pivot, received hereditary palace titles, and calmly accepted it without doubt—is this not Shi Ying?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for escort duty of the slightest kind, one man entered the Grand Secretariat, took control of the central administration, and accepted hereditary honors without a qualm—was that not Ma Shi Ying?

sentences.zh: 於是李沾侈言定策，挑激廷臣矣。

translations.literal: Thus Li Zhan extravagantly spoke of settling policy and provoked the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Zhan boasted of having settled the succession and goaded the court into factional strife.

sentences.zh: 劉孔昭以功賞不均，發憤冢臣，朝端嘩然聚訟，而群陰且翩翩起矣。

translations.literal: Liu Kongzhao, because rewards for merit were unequal, vented rage on the chief minister; the court end erupted in clamor and gathered litigation—and the swarm of yin forces began to rise lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kongzhao, angered by unequal rewards, turned his fury on the chief minister. The court erupted in uproar, and the dark faction began to stir.

sentences.zh: 借知兵之名，則逆黨可以然灰，寬反正之路，則逃臣可以汲引，而閣部諸臣且次第言去矣。

translations.literal: Borrowing the name of military knowledge, then rebels can be reduced to ash; widening the path of return to righteousness, then fleeing ministers can be drawn up—and the Grand Secretariat ministers will in turn speak of leaving one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking "military expertise" lets traitors off scot-free; opening the path to "surrender" welcomes back deserters—and ministers of the Grand Secretariat are resigning one after another.

sentences.zh: 中朝之黨論方興，何暇圖河北之賊？

translations.literal: Factional debate at the central court is just rising—what leisure to plan against the bandits of Hebei?
translations.idiomatic: With factional warfare consuming the court, who has time to fight the rebels in the north?

sentences.zh: 立國之本紀已疏，何以言匡攘之略？

translations.literal: The fundamental statutes of establishing the state are already lax—how speak of strategies to restore and expel?
translations.idiomatic: The foundations of the new state are already neglected—how can we speak of recovering the realm?

sentences.zh: 高傑一逃將也，而奉若驕子，浸有尾大之憂。

translations.literal: Gao Jie was a fleeing general, yet he was honored as a pampered son—gradually there was the worry of a tail growing too large.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie was a deserter, yet he was treated like a spoiled favorite—a growing threat to the throne.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚失事，不難譴撫臣道臣以謝之，安得不長其桀驁，則亦恃士英卵翼也。

translations.literal: When Huai and Yang lost affairs, it would not have been hard to reprimand the governor and circuit intendant to apologize to him—how could this not lengthen his arrogance and insolence? This too relied on Shi Ying's sheltering wings.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huai-Yang disaster, the court could easily have reprimanded the governor and circuit intendant to appease him—but that only fed his arrogance, shielded as he was by Ma Shi Ying's protection.

sentences.zh: 劉、黃諸將，各有舊汛地，而置若弈棋，洶洶為連雞之勢，至分剖江北四鎮以慰之，安得不啟其雄心，則皆高傑一人倡之也。

translations.literal: The generals Liu and Huang each had old garrison territories, yet they were set out like chess pieces, in uproar forming the momentum of linked chickens—until the four garrisons north of the river were divided to appease him; how could this not open their ambitious hearts? All were initiated by Gao Jie alone.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Liu and Huang each held established garrison posts, yet their territories were shuffled like chess pieces until mutual suspicion reigned. The four garrisons north of the river were carved up to appease Gao Jie—how could that not inflame their ambitions? He alone started it all.

sentences.zh: 京營自祖宗以來，皆勛臣為政，樞貳佐之。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Garrison, from the ancestors onward, has always been governed by meritorious ministers, with second-rank commissioners assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Metropolitan Garrison has been commanded by meritorious nobles, with senior officers as deputies.

sentences.zh: 陛下立國伊始，而有內臣盧九德之命，則士英有不得辭其責者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, at the very start of establishing the state, had the appointment of the inner attendant Lu Jiude—then Shi Ying cannot decline his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At the very founding of the state, Your Majesty appointed the eunuch Lu Jiude to command the Metropolitan Garrison—Ma Shi Ying cannot evade responsibility for that.

sentences.zh: 總之，兵戈盜賊，皆從小人氣類感召而生，而小人與奄宦又往往相表裏。

translations.literal: In sum, arms and banditry all arise from the mutual attraction of petty men's kind—and petty men and eunuchs often are outer and inner to each other.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, war and rebellion spring from the collusion of petty men—and petty men and eunuchs are invariably partners in crime.

sentences.zh: 自古未有奄宦用事，而將帥能樹功於方域者。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been eunuchs wielding power while generals could establish merit in the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history have eunuchs held power while generals won victories in the field.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下首辨陰陽消長之機，出士英仍督鳳陽，聯絡諸鎮，決用兵之策。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty first discern the mechanism of yin and yang waxing and waning: remove Shi Ying yet still have him supervise Fengyang, link the garrisons, and decide the policy of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to read the balance of power clearly: dismiss Ma Shi Ying but send him to supervise Fengyang, coordinate the garrisons, and settle on a military strategy.

sentences.zh: 史可法即不還中樞，亦當自淮而北，歷河以南，別開幕府，與士英相掎角。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa, even if not returning to the central pivot, should also from Huai go north, cross south of the river, separately open a headquarters, and with Shi Ying form pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Shi Kefa does not return to the central administration, he should march north from the Huai, cross the Yellow River, establish a separate command, and coordinate with Ma Shi Ying in a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 京營提督，獨斷寢之。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Garrison supervisor—solely decide to let it rest.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Metropolitan Garrison command—cancel that appointment outright.

sentences.zh: 書之史冊，為弘光第一美政。

translations.literal: Record it in the historical annals as the first fine policy of the Hongguang reign.
translations.idiomatic: Record it in the annals as the Hongguang era's first great act of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 王優詔答之，而促其速入。

translations.literal: The king replied with a gracious edict and urged him to enter quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict and urged him to come to court at once.

sentences.zh: 士英大怒，即日具疏辭位，且揚言於朝曰：「劉公自稱草莽孤臣，不書新命，明示不臣天子也。」

translations.literal: Shi Ying was greatly enraged; that very day he prepared a memorial resigning his post, and proclaimed in court, saying: "Lord Liu styled himself a lone minister of the wilds and did not write the new appointment—openly showing he will not serve the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying was furious. That same day he submitted his resignation and declared at court: "Lord Liu calls himself a private subject of the wilderness and omitted the new imperial title from his memorial—a plain refusal to acknowledge the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 其私人朱統𨰥遂劾宗周疏請移蹕鳳陽：「鳳陽，高墻所在，欲以罪宗處皇上，而與史可法擁立潞王。

translations.literal: His private man Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou's memorial requesting the transfer of the imperial residence to Fengyang: "Fengyang is where high walls stand; he wishes to place the emperor in the place of guilt, and with Shi Kefa to support and establish the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His client Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou for requesting that the court move to Fengyang: "Fengyang is a prison city. He means to confine the emperor there while he and Shi Kefa install the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 其兵已伏丹陽，當急備。」

translations.literal: His troops are already lying in ambush at Danyang—urgent preparations should be made."
translations.idiomatic: His troops are already hidden at Danyang. Guard against them at once."

sentences.zh: 而澤清、傑日夜謀所以殺宗周者不得，乃遣客十輩往刺宗周。

translations.literal: Yet Zeqing and Jie day and night schemed how to kill Zongzhou without success; then they sent ten batches of assassins to stab Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie plotted day and night to kill Zongzhou. Failing in that, they sent ten groups of assassins after him.

sentences.zh: 宗周時在丹陽，終日危坐，未嘗有惰容，客前後至者，不敢加害而去。

translations.literal: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day, never showing a lazy countenance; assassins who came before and after did not dare harm him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day without a trace of fear. Assassins came and went but none dared strike.

sentences.zh: 而黃鳴駿入覲，兵抵京口，與防江兵相擊鬥。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun entered audience; his troops reached Jingkou and clashed with the river-defense troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun came to court, and his troops reached Jingkou and fought with the river-defense forces.

sentences.zh: 士英以統𨰥言為信也，亦震恐。

translations.literal: Shi Ying took Tonglei's words as true and was also shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying, believing Zhu Tonglei's accusation, was terrified as well.

sentences.zh: 於是澤清疏劾：「宗周陰撓恢復，欲誅臣等，激變士心，召生靈之禍。」

translations.literal: Thus Zeqing memorialized in impeachment: "Zongzhou secretly obstructs recovery, wishes to execute us ministers, stirs mutiny in soldiers' hearts, and summons calamity upon the people."
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Zeqing memorialized: "Zongzhou secretly sabotages the recovery effort, seeks to execute us, inflames the troops, and invites disaster upon the people."

sentences.zh: 劉良佐亦具疏言宗周力持「三案」，為門戶主盟，倡議親征，圖晁錯之自為居守，司馬懿之閉城拒君。

translations.literal: Liu Liangzuo also prepared a memorial saying Zongzhou forcefully upheld the "Three Cases," acted as factional chief, advocated personal campaign, and schemed Chao Cuo's staying behind to hold the fort and Sima Yi's closing the gates to reject the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liangzuo also submitted a memorial accusing Zongzhou of championing the "Three Cases," leading the factional alliance, and urging a personal campaign—plotting, like Chao Cuo, to hold power while the emperor marched, and, like Sima Yi, to shut the gates against the throne.

sentences.zh: 疏未下，澤清復草一疏，署傑、良佐及黃得功名上之，言：「宗周勸上親征，謀危君父，欲安置陛下於烽火兇危之地。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was issued, Zeqing again drafted a memorial, signed by Jie, Liangzuo, and Huang Degong and submitted it, saying: "Zongzhou urged the sovereign to personally campaign, schemed peril to the sovereign and father, and wished to place Your Majesty in a place of beacon fires and fierce danger.
translations.idiomatic: Before that memorial was even issued, Liu Zeqing drafted another, signed by Gao Jie, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong, declaring: "Zongzhou urged Your Majesty to lead the campaign personally, endangering the throne, and meant to place you in the midst of battle and peril.

sentences.zh: 蓋非宗周一人之謀，姜曰廣、吳甡合謀也。

translations.literal: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen conspired together.
translations.idiomatic: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen were his co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 曰廣心雄膽大，翊戴非其本懷，故陰結死黨，翦除諸忠，然後迫劫乘輿，遷之別郡。

translations.literal: Yueguang's heart was bold and his courage great; supporting the enthronement was not his original intent—thus he secretly bound a diehard faction, cut down the loyal, and then coerced the imperial carriage and moved it to another commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang is ambitious and bold; enthroning the emperor was never his true aim. He secretly formed a faction, purged the loyal, and then meant to seize the imperial carriage and relocate the court.

sentences.zh: 如甡、宗周入都，臣等即渡江赴闕，面訐諸奸，正《春秋》討賊之義。」

translations.literal: If Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we ministers will immediately cross the river and go to the palace, face-to-face denounce the traitors, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 righteousness of punishing rebels."
translations.idiomatic: If Wu Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we shall cross the Yangtze, appear before the throne, denounce these traitors face to face, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 principle of punishing rebels."

sentences.zh: 疏入，舉朝大駭，傳諭和衷集事。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the whole court was greatly alarmed; an edict was transmitted urging harmony of heart and gathering of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court was horrified. An edict was issued calling for harmony and unity.

sentences.zh: 宗周不得已，以七月十八日入朝。

translations.literal: Zongzhou had no choice; on the eighteenth day of the seventh month he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou had no choice but to enter court on the eighteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 初，澤清疏出，遣人錄示傑。

translations.literal: At first, when Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent someone to copy and show it to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent a copy to Gao Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑曰：「我輩武人，乃預朝事耶？」

translations.literal: Jie said: "We military men—are we to participate in court affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie said: "We are soldiers—since when do we meddle in court affairs?"

sentences.zh: 得功疏辨：「臣不預聞。」

translations.literal: Degong submitted a memorial in defense: "Your subject did not participate in hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong submitted a defense: "Your subject had no part in this."

sentences.zh: 士英寢不奏。

translations.literal: Shi Ying shelved it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying suppressed it and never forwarded it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 可法不平，遣使遍詰諸鎮，咸云不知，遂據以入告，澤清輩由是氣沮。

translations.literal: Kefa was indignant; he sent envoys to question all the garrisons everywhere—they all said they did not know—then relied on this to enter and report, and Zeqing and company thereby lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa, indignant, sent envoys to question every garrison. All denied knowledge of the plot. He reported this to the throne, and Liu Zeqing and his allies lost heart.
